title: Geometry - Lesson 1 Practice: Tessellation Hunt
description: Practice identifying repeating shape patterns, examples of tessellations, and non-examples with gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a tessellation?
options: A repeating pattern that covers a flat surface with no gaps and no overlaps
Any picture that uses many colors
A pattern that repeats but leaves empty spaces
A shape that has exactly four sides
questions.explanation: A tessellation must repeat and cover the surface completely without gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: A pattern made of repeated circles with spaces between the circles is a tessellation.
questions.explanation: The circles repeat, but the spaces between them are gaps. A tessellation cannot have gaps.

questions.question: A floor is covered by same-size square tiles arranged edge-to-edge. What is the best classification?
options: Not a tessellation because squares have corners
Not a tessellation because tiles repeat
Not enough information because all floor patterns are random
questions.explanation: Square tiles arranged edge-to-edge cover the surface with no gaps or overlaps, so the design is a tessellation.

questions.question: A tessellation has no gaps and no ______.
questions.explanation: The two main visual checks are no gaps and no overlaps.

questions.question: Which situation is most likely a tessellation?
options: A honeycomb pattern made of hexagons with no spaces between them
A row of stars printed across the top of a page
Circles repeated on a background with white spaces between them
Two triangles drawn on top of each other
questions.explanation: Hexagons can fit edge-to-edge like a honeycomb, leaving no gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: In one sentence, explain why a repeating pattern with overlaps is not a tessellation.
questions.correctAnswer: A repeating pattern with overlaps is not a tessellation because shapes cover the same space, and tessellations must cover each part of the surface exactly once.
questions.explanation: Overlaps break the rule that the surface should be covered cleanly, with each part covered once.

questions.question: A tessellation can use more than one kind of shape.
questions.explanation: A tessellation may use one shape or a repeated group of shapes, as long as there are no gaps or overlaps.

questions.question: Name one real-life place where you might see a tessellation.
questions.correctAnswer: floor tiles, wall tiles, woven mats, textiles, fabric patterns, mosaics, or brick walls
questions.explanation: Tessellations often appear in tiled floors, textile patterns, mosaics, woven mats, and brick patterns.
